scope: Local repair requested after the shared skinned character release: narrower softer lower jaw, rounded chin and more natural teeth. Both FORM and MUSE retain the same identity.
reviewers: Root: actual before/after frontal, profile and three-quarter neutral renders, then expression extremes.
FORM integration agent: independent before/after neutral contour review.

appliedSculpt.method: Fixed lower-face taper and rounded chin; transported morphs and normals

repairs: Increased the native lateral jaw morph modestly, and added a fixed smooth taper at the lower cheek/mandibular corners.
Rounded and slightly shortened the chin while preserving its forward projection and the original upper face.
Transported attached accessory positions, expression displacements and normals through the same local sculpt.
Refined licensed crown proportions and incisal edges in the separate dental module; balanced oral exposure in expression recipes.
rejectedTrial: Large native jaw/chin reduction weights changed depth more than width and made the profile recede; reduced those weights and used a local lateral contour instead.
observations: The lower-face silhouette is visibly slimmer than the archived baseline. The chin remains rounded rather than pointed or recessed.
The neutral front/profile/three-quarter views retain the same eyes, nose, hair and overall character identity.
No new cheek pinch, jaw-to-neck crease or detached facial boundary was observed in the reviewed neutral captures.

Root reviewed the final frontal peak contact sheet for all eight expressions and individual fear, surprise and laughter captures after the oral-pose change. Lower teeth are less exposed, and the smile retains individual upper crowns.
limitations: This is sampled visual self-review of an illustrative realtime character, not clinical validation or a photographic likeness.
The skin and textured hair retain the existing game-asset finish.
